assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks turned atomic frequency standards into extraordinarily precise tools for fundamental physics and precision measurement. This is a major, sustained advance in atomic physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori and Ye made distinct, seminal contributions to the lattice clock approach and its experimental realization.
assessment.maturity: The technology has been repeatedly demonstrated and refined across laboratories, with clear scientific uses beyond timekeeping.
uncertainties: The boundary between the foundational clock contributions and the broader community's later advances would need careful definition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Horizon-scale imaging converted black-hole structure from a theoretical and indirect subject into an observable one, through a striking achievement in interferometry and data analysis.
assessment.attribution: Falcke helped establish the scientific case, Moran contributed foundational very-long-baseline interferometry expertise, and Doeleman led key observational efforts. Their roles span important parts of the achievement.
assessment.maturity: The image has been independently scrutinized and followed by further observations, though the technique and observational program continue to develop.
uncertainties: The result depended on a large international collaboration, so selecting a small number of individuals risks leaving out essential contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Precision maps of the cosmic microwave background made anisotropies a quantitative foundation for modern cosmology and constrained the universe's composition and history.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Page represent central experimental leadership in mapping, while Spergel contributed significantly to interpreting the cosmological implications.
assessment.maturity: The measurements have been extended and cross-checked by later missions, and their scientific consequences are deeply established.
uncertainties: This description spans multiple missions and scientific roles; the relative credit for the maps themselves versus their interpretation needs sharper boundaries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The self-amplified spontaneous-emission free-electron laser enabled intense, ultrashort X-ray pulses and opened new ways to study matter at atomic and molecular scales.
assessment.attribution: Pellegrini, Saldin, and Kim are associated with complementary conceptual and technical contributions to the SASE approach.
assessment.maturity: Operational X-ray free-electron lasers have established the method's scientific value and sustained impact.
uncertainties: The path from theory to operating facilities involved many contributors, and the individual division of credit is not fully clear from this candidate description.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics established powerful ways to couple light to mechanical motion, probe quantum behavior in larger systems, and approach measurement limits.
assessment.attribution: Vahala, Aspelmeyer, and Kippenberg are prominent contributors to the field's development, spanning resonator physics and experimental demonstrations.
assessment.maturity: There is a substantial body of reproducible work, but several of the field's most ambitious quantum-control goals remain active research.
uncertainties: The discovery is broad and cumulative, making it difficult to identify a single prize-sized result and a uniquely bounded set of contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Foundational proposals for quantum computing and simulation with trapped ions and neutral atoms helped turn quantum information into a concrete experimental program.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made closely connected theoretical contributions that shaped architectures and methods later realized in laboratories.
assessment.maturity: The experimental platforms are now powerful and well established, although scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computing remains unfinished.
uncertainties: The proposed discovery combines foundations and platforms whose later experimental advances involved many independent groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light makes quantum noise a controllable resource and enables precision measurements beyond the standard quantum limit, with direct relevance to gravitational-wave detection.
assessment.attribution: Caves provided key theoretical foundations, Kimble advanced influential experimental implementations, and Schnabel represents important later demonstrations and applications.
assessment.maturity: The technique has moved into large-scale instruments and continues to improve their sensitivity.
uncertainties: The candidate combines foundational theory with experimental development over several decades, so the appropriate scope and credit allocation are debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry brought coherent matter waves into precision inertial and fundamental-constant measurements, creating a versatile measurement method.
assessment.attribution: Bordé, Pritchard, and Kasevich are associated with foundational concepts and influential demonstrations, though the method grew through broad international work.
assessment.maturity: The technique is experimentally mature and used across atomic physics and metrology, while new applications and performance improvements continue.
uncertainties: The candidate groups several measurement applications and generations of instruments; the central contribution and individual credit would need clearer definition.
